notes: EBIT is proxied as GAAP operating income from the consolidated statements of income. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/385562537/files/doc_financials/2026/TYL-12-31-2025-10K-vF.pdf))

D&A is proxied as consolidated 'Depreciation and amortization' from the consolidated cash flow statement. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/385562537/files/doc_financials/2026/TYL-12-31-2025-10K-vF.pdf))

Capex is defined as total cash outflows for (1) additions to property and equipment plus (2) investment in software development (capitalized internally developed software). This definition is consistent with the cash flow line items used in Tyler’s statements. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/385562537/files/doc_financials/2026/TYL-12-31-2025-10K-vF.pdf))

NWC is constructed as: (Total current assets - cash and cash equivalents - short-term investments) - (Total current liabilities - current debt). Current debt is proxied by the 'current portion' of the company’s debt line item (term loans in FY2023; convertible notes current portion in FY2025). This construction is a modeling choice; lease liabilities and deferred revenue remain embedded in current assets/liabilities. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/385562537/files/doc_financials/2026/TYL-12-31-2025-10K-vF.pdf))

tax_rate is set to 0.23 based on Tyler’s non-GAAP tax rate expectation for 2026 referenced in the earnings release; it may differ from GAAP effective tax in historical periods. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/385562537/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/26-7-Q4-earnings-PR.pdf))
WACC is assumed (0.09) rather than directly sourced from filings; it is an input needed for the DCF pipeline. Terminal value uses Gordon growth (terminal_exit_ebitda_multiple set null).

nol_balance is taken as the after-tax federal/state net operating loss and net tax credit carryforwards of $5.3M disclosed as of Dec 31, 2025 (this is not necessarily the gross pre-tax NOL amount). ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/385562537/files/doc_financials/2026/TYL-12-31-2025-10K-vF.pdf))

Peer comps: forward P/E is populated where available from captured StockAnalysis outputs; EV/NTM revenue and EV/NTM EBITDA were not captured in the retrieved outputs and are set null. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/pltr/statistics/))

catalysts: Follow-through on converting customers to SaaS (subscription/SaaS growth and SaaS flip activity referenced in the earnings release). ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/385562537/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/26-7-Q4-earnings-PR.pdf))

Sustained execution against FY2026 guidance amid public-sector budget cycles, with potential for upward revisions if conversion and transaction revenue remain resilient. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/385562537/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/26-7-Q4-earnings-PR.pdf))

Integration and earnings contribution from acquisitions (e.g., CloudGavel and Edulink referenced in the Q4/FY2025 release). ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/385562537/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/26-7-Q4-earnings-PR.pdf))
company_overview: Tyler Technologies provides integrated software and technology services to the U.S. public sector across enterprise and platform solutions, as well as transaction-based services. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/385562537/files/doc_financials/2026/TYL-12-31-2025-10K-vF.pdf))

Revenue mix is increasingly recurring, supported by SaaS subscriptions and maintenance arrangements, with a material share of subscription and SaaS revenues. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/385562537/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/26-7-Q4-earnings-PR.pdf))

The company’s scale and recurring contract base support high operating margins and strong operating cash generation. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/385562537/files/doc_financials/2026/TYL-12-31-2025-10K-vF.pdf))
current_context: FY2025: total revenues of $2.332B (+9.1% YoY), GAAP operating income of $357.7M, and free cash flow of $620.8M. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/385562537/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/26-7-Q4-earnings-PR.pdf))

Feb 11, 2026 guidance: FY2026 total revenues of $2.50B–$2.55B and capital expenditures of $24M–$26M (including ~$10M of capitalized software development costs). ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/385562537/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/26-7-Q4-earnings-PR.pdf))

4Q/SaaS momentum: SaaS revenues grew 20.6% to $777.8M for FY2025 (and SaaS revenue growth exceeded 20% in the quarter referenced in the release). ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/385562537/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/26-7-Q4-earnings-PR.pdf))
investment_highlights: Base-case thesis assumes continued SaaS mix improvement and durability of recurring revenues, supporting gradual EBIT margin expansion from recent levels. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/385562537/files/doc_financials/2026/TYL-12-31-2025-10K-vF.pdf))

Capex discipline is guided by 2026 expectations (notably lower than 2024–2025 total capitalized software + property additions), supporting improving FCF conversion in the model. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/385562537/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/26-7-Q4-earnings-PR.pdf))

Working-capital dynamics have been structurally negative in recent history under the modeled NWC construction, and base-case assumes continued stability. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/385562537/files/doc_financials/2026/TYL-12-31-2025-10K-vF.pdf))

DCF incorporates a terminal framework consistent with a durable software-like earnings profile (Gordon growth) rather than an exit-multiple assumption. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/385562537/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/26-7-Q4-earnings-PR.pdf))
key_risks: Government entity budget pressure could slow transaction volumes and SaaS conversion pace, impacting revenue growth assumptions. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/385562537/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/26-7-Q4-earnings-PR.pdf))

Margin pressure from mix shifts, hosting costs, amortization of intangibles from acquisitions, or higher operating expenses could reduce EBIT margin path. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/385562537/files/doc_financials/2026/TYL-12-31-2025-10K-vF.pdf))

Working-capital swings (collections timing and contract-related liabilities) could diverge from the modeled NWC-to-sales stability. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/385562537/files/doc_financials/2026/TYL-12-31-2025-10K-vF.pdf))
